output_list.reason: The mintToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When the owner calls mintToken, the amount of tokens to be minted is added to the target's balance without a check, allowing the balance of the contract to become extremely large, and in turn, allowing the owner to drain funds from the contract.

The transfer function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When the balanceOf[_to] + _value < balanceOf[_to] is evaluated, if _value is large enough, it can cause an overflow, making this evaluation always true, and in turn, allowing attackers to steal funds from any user.

The transferFrom function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When the balanceOf[_to] + _value < balanceOf[_to] is evaluated, if _value is large enough, it can cause an overflow, making this evaluation always true, and in turn, allowing attackers to steal funds from any user.

The buy function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When the amount of tokens to be bought is calculated, if the buyPrice is set to a very small value, attackers can overflow the amount variable, causing it to be zero, and in turn, allowing attackers to steal funds from the contract.

The sell function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When the amount * sellPrice is evaluated, if the attackers can control the sellPrice, attackers can overflow the amount variable, causing it to be zero, and in turn, allowing attackers to steal funds from the user.
